verdict.rationale: Blocking tracking pixels and being transparent about mail-data use are fair questions for an email client like Outlook, so the axis applies. However, the evidence pack contains nothing on blocking remote images or read pixels by default, and no privacy or data-use disclosures. The docs cover Graph mail APIs, and the community items discuss link handling, performance and ads, none of which documents this capability.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data
